sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
Kal'tsit, Medic Operator of Rhodes Island. After a brief and unexpected parting, she has returned.

She lost her eternal life, and gained everything that belongs to ordinary people — all the pain, the imperfection, and the hope.

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A dose of Oripathy suppressant, the latest achievement of Rhodes Island's Medical Department. Not yet a cure that removes all suffering — but it is her answer to the promise she made to herself.

sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Kal'tsit, one of the founders of Rhodes Island Pharmaceuticals, concurrently serving as head of the Medical Department. She has led Rhodes Island's large-scale strategic operations on numerous occasions and has been responsible for Rhodes Island's external communications, making significant contributions to the company's operational development and to Oripathy research. She now takes part in Rhodes Island's Oripathy pharmaceutical research and development program primarily in the capacity of a medical specialist.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Kal'tsit shows no signs of infection at this time.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.07u/L
As of the time of examination, Operator Kal'tsit has rarely come into contact with Originium.

Yes—Kal'tsit has at last agreed to submit to a physical. Nearly eight years after the founding of Rhodes Island's Medical Department, we have finally established the physical condition of the department's own head. This is a major advance in our work, and cause for congratulation. Yet for some reason, watching Kal'tsit affect an air of complete indifference, as though all those obstinate moments in the past had never happened at all, I suddenly felt far less of a sense of achievement. In any case, while drawing her blood, I was finally able to confirm that she is not a cold-blooded animal.
Setting aside for the moment the underlying principles of the sarcophagus's mysterious technology and looking only at her examination results: apart from how little contact she has had with Originium, virtually every metric falls just barely short of the point where it would cause concern, yet can still be counted as healthy. There is nothing extreme anywhere, which is reassuring on another level entirely. How should I put it... it is as though she were an 'ordinary person.'
—Warfarin

From now on, leave her physicals to me.
——Mon3tr

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
After that accident, for a number of reasons, the losses Rhodes Island had suffered were not immediately relayed to every Operator—Kal'tsit's 'death' included.
Apart from the Elite Operators and a very small number of Senior Operators, the vast majority of Operators who had already left Rhodes Island at the time knew nothing of that grievous upheaval. So when they returned to Rhodes Island's new base, the only thing that surprised them was how completely the place had been made over. Some may well have wondered about a mysterious girl who had appeared out of nowhere and yet turned up constantly in the Medical Department—and about a Kal'tsit who seemed just a little different.
Just how was she different? Naturally, some were curious enough to ask about the strange piece of medical equipment she now carried with her, and Kal'tsit would explain frankly that it was an instrument for monitoring her own physical condition. Was Dr. Kal'tsit ill? She did look somewhat frail. Beyond urging her to take care of herself, no one said much more. Before long, however, the rumor that 'Dr. Kal'tsit's change in temperament is apparently due to a severe deterioration of her condition' reached her ears after all.
We are all confident that no Operator who knows Kal'tsit could fail to hold this doctor in respect. As for how the rumor arose, it was more than anything because everyone genuinely cared about Kal'tsit's physical condition. On this point, Kal'tsit herself has indicated that no special explanation is necessary.
Many Operators have noticed that at some point Kal'tsit stopped appearing frequently in the operations meeting room, while opportunities to run into her in the Medical Department have grown far more numerous. She now devotes more of her time to advancing the Oripathy pharmaceutical development project and to instructing the younger Medic Operators—which is, of course, a fine thing for Medic Operators still in training. Kal'tsit's work ethic, unchanged from before, has gradually put everyone at ease. As for the rumor of 'Dr. Kal'tsit's change in temperament,' let us simply say that once a person no longer has to divide their energies among so many concerns, their disposition really does improve.

'But I honestly think Instructor Kal'tsit looks better with long hair. She seems a little gentler that way.'
'Are you out of your mind?! That is not a topic for working hours! Not even if it happens to be the consensus!'

[Classified Log]
'Continuing the discussion from the last Elite Operator meeting, our final decision is this: what Rhodes Island encountered in Rim Billiton and our operations in Ursus will remain at the highest level of confidentiality... As for Dr. Kal'tsit's physical condition, perhaps that is a secret not worth deliberately concealing or explaining. All we need to do is let everyone know—she is still here, together with Rhodes Island. That is enough.'
- Amiya

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
The sarcophagus—yes. You saw those pasts, and you came to know its place in history.
Those bygone events are each a microcosm, identical in every respect to our present circumstances. We have reason enough to be disappointed—to conclude that people never learned sufficient lessons from history, and let those tragedies and sufferings repeat themselves. Across all that time, people never wholly conquered the darker side of their own nature. But by the same token, they were never defeated by that suffering either.
The sarcophagus cannot save Ursus from the Originium cataclysm; it is no antidote to Terra's many crises. What it did do, at the very least, was give me—and you—a second life. That is precisely the result of our having chosen hope.
The disaster grows more severe with every passing minute and second. There is no more time left for us to grieve.
……
With the Zelgrad mission concluded, Deity Grypherburg will not be satisfied with the present outcome—at least, not everyone there will be. Witte's tacit consent to our extricating ourselves from the chaos in Zelgrad is a friendly signal; we will need more contact still. At the same time, however, Rhodes Island's name is certain to appear in the reports of every army.
Doctor, if you are asking for my advice, we discussed this back when we left Londinium. Rhodes Island cannot maintain the political detachment it once had—and the same holds for what has happened in Ursus.
There's no need to sound me out so cautiously. From the Far North's mining district to Zelgrad, you and Amiya led Rhodes Island to remarkable achievements. I could not have done better than the two of you. You should be proud, and you should trust your own judgment more.
Yes, we have grounds to conclude that the Ursus authorities no longer have the capacity to resolve their own internal conflicts, and that the most pessimistic—and most likely—outcome is for those conflicts to escalate into bloodshed directed outward. The cataclysm unfolding in Ursus is without question a crisis belonging to all of Terra. In this crisis brought on by Originium, Rhodes Island can still do more.
We must return to Ursus after all.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
We studied, as far as we were able, the theory Mon3tr shared with us regarding the sarcophagus—or rather, the 'home-use life functions restoration device.' By her account this was already a textbook edition of her own translation, yet after no small amount of effort we abandoned outright any intention of fully comprehending such impenetrable material.
By our 'shallow' biological theory, the present Kal'tsit—a life form that might almost be said to have 'appeared out of thin air'—defies all common sense. It is very nearly a scene out of any number of myths: a lifelike doll or statue turned into a 'person' by the touch of a god. Yet the endings of such stories are almost without exception the same: these newborn 'people' are in the end deprived of life by that same god. Such myths reflect certain fundamental ethical convictions held by people—namely, that life must not be created by any means outside natural procreation. It may be a groundless worry, but we do worry that such a plot might genuinely play out in reality. And all we can do is keep watch over her physical condition.
We compared the physical examination results of the present Kal'tsit and of Mon3tr side by side. The conclusion was that Mon3tr's physical attributes far exceed the range of an ordinary Terran in many respects—absurdly high muscle and bone density, for instance, and an immune system enviably robust. Kal'tsit, on the other hand, by every means of medical testing available to us, is in all respects entirely indistinguishable from an ordinary Terran human. That means she will fall ill, she will age, and at some point in the future she will meet an unavoidable death. Yet no one can quite explain why, upon confirming that these perfectly self-evident things really will happen to Kal'tsit, a strange feeling stirred in all of our hearts.
Perhaps an indestructible Kal'tsit was only ever our own wishful expectation. And from now on, Rhodes Island will protect her as well.

>TIMEDATA 1102/02/01
>ADMIN: Mon3tr; Kal'tsit·Esperanta
What the Doctor does not yet know is that the original intent of the AMa-10 project was for the individual designated AMa-10 to serve, after the Silence descended, as a mass-produced multipurpose machine assisting the surviving humans in rebuilding their homes. And in order to satisfy that design purpose, one of the most basic requirements was that AMa-10 must not be identified as a life form by ■■■.
In other words, although AMa-10 possesses powerful biomimetic capabilities and can simulate very nearly every physiological behavior of a living being, at the level of fundamental definition AMa-10 is not regarded as life.
But by the same token, an AMa-10 individual that severed its own gemini cycle and went on surviving was in no one's original expectations.
'Kal'tsit, what am I now—what are you now... exactly?'
'There is no one from whom we can simply demand an answer. The origin of life is a riddle even the previous civilization never cracked.'
'Still, we may keep this question. It is worth continuing to seek after... Let us carry the doubt with us and keep walking.'

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
Our communication can finally proceed without restriction now. That has never once been the case before.
What else would you like to know? I have no secrets left now, do I?
If you wish, I am willing to share what I saw and heard in the past with you—though I make no guarantee whatsoever that any of it will sound interesting.
I have held many identities—tyrant, prophet, monk, warrior... Each identity stood for an attempt, an attempt to stop a fledgling civilization from destroying itself. Behind every one of them, the only thing that never changed was the name 'Kal'tsit.' That name alone could remind me to remember who I am.
It was you who handed it to me... no, to be precise, the individual then called the Oracle—though in truth I could never be certain, even at the very end, whether what that person handed me was a mission or a choice.
To become the guardian of civilization, and to find myself—these were two directives running in opposite directions. No one can possess meaning and freedom at once. I tried to reconcile the two, but I never arrived at a reasonable answer.
What I did end up with, however, was a 'wish.'
I hope to see Terra's more distant future—people breaking the shackles of the barrier, mending the rifts between races and nations, even crossing that veil of Silence. And what lies beyond it? Of course I do not know... But I want to know.
And I hope that in that future, traces of Rhodes Island will still remain.
You look rather at ease, Doctor. I'm glad you take an optimistic view of this as well—that's not what you meant? You're saying...
...I'm smiling?

First: all language and writing, in the broad sense, arose from life's need to transmit information—a need that in fact implies the instinctive conviction, held by primitive living individuals, that they themselves can be understood.
Second: grounded in the basic needs common to all life, every language shares a common underlying structure.
Third: language and thought influence one another, and so different individuals cannot truly reach a consensus of thought through different languages.
……
Kal'tsit tells you that this is a doctrine called the 'Esperanta Principle,' proposed by a certain linguist in the very distant past. It was on the basis of this theory that he devoted his life to inventing a complete language, one as universally usable between different civilizations as possible. He firmly believed that in that age of war and turmoil, such an endeavor would help people dissolve their differences.
After returning to Rhodes Island, Kal'tsit chose 'Kal'tsit·Esperanta' as her full name. In that language, which was never completed, the word also means 'hope.'

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Though you will no longer remember it.
This universe once nurtured a brilliant civilization. In that age, the boundary of knowledge was very nearly coextensive with the universe itself. Human cognition could reach into every corner of the imaginable; even the most distant star was as close at hand as a book upon the desk.
And yet even so, people could not answer the question concerning themselves—does life possess some purpose innate to it?
Perhaps this is the last veil the Creator left behind: the search for meaning has no exit, and life is destined to walk toward solitude on each of its own journeys.

In the end, the philosophers and scholars gave up seeking answers in the observable world, and chose instead to place their faith in our instincts.
Because we can only believe that, beyond the insoluble solitude and confusion, the existence of love is equally beyond doubt.
Not even the deepest despair could stop people from searching the vast sea of stars for an echo of their own existence. Before the Silence descended, people still wept over traces of life tens of thousands of light-years away.
I think that on my journey I have finally come to understand that emotion. Life is beautiful; on the scale of the universe, 'life' and 'hope' mean the same thing.

I cannot give you back the memories of the past. All I can do is try to share with you what I have felt.
I will trust your nature, and I hope that you can trust the meaning of what you have chosen.
You will feel helpless and lost, because no one can walk beside you forever, and no one can understand your loneliness.
Rhodes Island has become a home to many. I hope that, when that time comes, Rhodes Island can be a place for you to belong as well.
My wish is to safeguard your wish. I hope that when this journey ends, there will be someone at your side to witness the future you have been waiting for.

A voice message, stored at some unknown point in the archive of your terminal.
The first time you saw these words, Rhodes Island was throwing all its efforts into preparing the rescue mission bound for Ursus, and there was not much time left for you to grieve or to think. After Kal'tsit returned safely to Rhodes Island, the two of you likewise refrained, by tacit understanding, from mentioning that the message existed.
Yet this singular letter ended up remaining far longer than you had imagined.

'The ones who left their names on these gravestones—who were they?'
'They were all... the cornerstones of civilization.'
